title: Housing Management System - Newark and Sherwood District Council
description:
Newark and Sherwood District Council wishes to invite tenders for the supply of services in respect of the provision and configuration of a cloud-based housing management system with ongoing support and product updates throughout the contract lifespan.
 
The aims/objectives/service priorities of this contract are:
•             Provision and ongoing support of a cloud-based housing management system that will capture information relating to social housing tenancy management, application management and bidding. 
•             Implementation services including configuration and training
•             Data mapping support
 
The contract will commence from 1st April 2023 and will contain implementations phases to prepare for the system launch.  The Council requires the provision of parallel runs to compare with the existing system to ensure of complete accuracy prior to sign off.
 
Newark and Sherwood District Council owns over 5,500 properties along with additional asset types that will be managed through the system.  User information for licences is contained within the specification.
 
The Requirement if for a maximum term of 120 months (10 years) with the core contract for 60 months, subject to agreement to extend once for a further 60 months.
 
Following on from the advertisements in Find a Tender Service and Contracts Finder, bidders must express interest, access the tender documentation and submit bids within the ProContract system at https://www.eastmidstenders.org/ using reference DN641903.  The submission process includes 2 online questionnaires which must be submitted within the system only.

title: TENDER FOR WORKS TO 14 MARKET PLACE NEWARK AND SHERWOOD DISTRICT COUNCIL
description:
Newark and Sherwood District Council wishes to invite tenders for the supply of works in respect of the refurbishment of 14 Market Place to return it into daily use and to ensure the future use of the building remains known and within the council's control. Market Place sits in a prominent location in the town centre of Newark with a dual frontage onto the Market Place and Queens Head Court. It is a building of significant visual interest and contributes to the character of the Market Place. It is comprised of a large basement, ground floor retail space and former residential space spread over the upper three floors.\r
\r
Bidders interested in the opportunity are invited to apply using the ProContract e-tendering portal, searching for project number DN737172. The deadline for tenders is 12 noon 6th September 2024.\r

title: 9121 Newark Town Centre Masterplan and Design Code - AWARD
description: This brief is issued on behalf of Newark and Sherwood District Council (NSDC) and Historic England, who wish to appoint a multi-disciplinary team to develop a deliverable masterplan and design code that ensures Newark Town Centre is a place that drives economic growth and ensures future sustainability, whilst sustaining the significance and value of the town's rich history and character. The boundary for the Masterplan should include the inner town centre area, key transport nodes and opportunity sites for development and address the whole of the Newark Town Centre Conservation Area and other land necessary to establish a successful strategy. Key issues that will need to be addressed include informing planning for movement around the town centre and transport interventions, enabling infill, backland and larger regeneration projects, appropriate land uses across the town centre reflecting aspirations for a resilient mixed-use economy, physical and non-physical interventions and ensuring that the new development is designed to reflect variation in character across the masterplan area.

title: BP1031 - Housing Benefit Subsidy Assurance Services
description:
Broxtowe Borough Council is conducting the procurement exercise on behalf of the Council's listed below, to establish contracts for the supply of Housing Benefit Assurance Services.

•	Broxtowe Borough Council
•	Gedling Borough Council
•	Newark and Sherwood District Council 
•	Rushcliffe Borough Council
(The Council/s)

Each of the participating Councils will award contracts separately and day-to-day transactions under the agreement will be conducted between the appointed Service Provider (Auditor) and the particular Council concerned. In any event, any formal contracts which emerge from this process will be entered into separately with the Service Provider by each council, with no relationship of joint or several liabilities between them.

The Council requires a Service Provider (Auditor) to audit their Housing Benefit (HB) Subsidy Grant claims in England, commencing with the subsidy period 1 April 2023 to 31 March 2024. (equivalent dates for any extension period), to meet the Department of Work and Pensions (DWP) requirements to give the DWP assurance of a valid and true claim. The Service Provider will conduct testing of all Housing Benefit Assurance Procedure (HBAP) aspects of the audit.

Bidders must be currently registered on the Local Public Audit Register and available to facilitate the HBAP in respect of the FYE ending March 2023 and FYE March 2024, as detailed in the LA Welfare Direct Bulletin - LAWD 12/2022, otherwise your bid will fail.

The initial contract period is 12 months. The contract is estimated to commence 1 April 2024 and expire 31 March 2025.

There will be an option to extend the contract for 24 months in 12 month increments, subject to satisfactory performance and business needs. Maximum contract period is 36 months, covering 2023, 2024 and 2025 audit requirements

Please visit the Council's e-tendering system https://www.eastmidstenders.org where you can express interest and obtain the documents, (please note we will only accept expressions of interest through the e-tendering system). Please search for BP1031.

title: Safe Accommodation Support Services for Women (Refuges)
description:
This project was a further competition procedure under the dynamic purchasing system Domestic Abuse Safe Accommodation Support Services Dynamic Provider List, project reference DN571003. It was run in accordance with the Public Contract Regulations 2015 and was a Light Touch Procurement for social and other specific services.
To ensure the appropriate types and coverage of refuge provision across the County bids were sought for three Lots.
LOT 1, South Nottinghamshire, covers Ashfield district and Broxtowe, Gedling and Rushcliffe boroughs.  The requirement was for communal accommodation, with or without additional dispersed accommodation.
LOT 2, Countywide required dispersed accommodation across the County of Nottinghamshire.
LOT 3, North Nottinghamshire, covers Mansfield, Newark and Sherwood and Bassetlaw districts.  The requirement was for communal accommodation, with or without additional dispersed accommodation.
The aim of the services is to provide comprehensive specialist support services for female survivors of domestic abuse and their children residing in domestic abuse safe accommodation.  This will include ensuring the highest degree of safety and security for survivors residing in the accommodation, offering individual support to meet the assessed needs of Survivors and aid their recovery, supporting Survivors to access other services to meet their physical and mental health needs, supporting Survivors and encouraging them to make independent decisions about their lives and being responsive to the needs of children and young people, ensuring they receive the right support to deal with the trauma they have endured.
Services will be delivered within safe accommodation, refuges, which may be individual units, dispersed housing or communal refuges.

title: Asset Based Community Development Study
description:
To undertake an Asset Based Community Development (ABCD) Study that will result in a strong evidence base that will inform activities and investment required to deliver against the Council's Community Plan, Health and Wellbeing Strategy, Housing Strategy and Economic Growth Strategy. The study will focus on a number of key areas within the Newark and Sherwood Local Authority District, 

The study will provide evidence to support future funding bids / applications to assist with the levelling up agenda and substantial information to develop a community engagement and regeneration plan and supports the creation of vibrant and self-sufficient local communities where residents look out for each other and actively contribute to their local area. 

Adopting the ABCD approach allows the council to develop a sustainable model for community development focused on the strengths and potential within a community. The project will develop our 'place based' working with partners to identify and develop a strengths-based register of community assets in a locality - covering both physical assets and individuals, groups and networks who contribute to sustainable, thriving communities.
